digest.component_or_area: BindingStore module and binding persistence layer
propositions: BindingStore's 799-line module owns too many concerns (byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, comment identity, rotation, publication) with no cohesive internal architecture and no clear owner for new safety rules

Production code mutates live bindings returned by shallow all_bindings() query, creating risk of silent data loss and regression in crash recovery, identity deduplication, and selective publication behavior

Extract three internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, recovery) behind a stable public facade while preserving all existing serialization, unknown-field handling, and method compatibility

Implement journal-free retirement completion rule: a durable tombstone is authoritative intent and live pairs are removed only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree; only explicit unretire revokes that intent
Recovery must run after configuration snapshot and exclusive lock validation but before remote issue fetch and binding walk, preventing interleaving of new liveness evidence with completion
Load, check, dry-run, preview, and filtered operations must not trigger recovery writes; only validated write-bearing operations may repair interrupted retirements
